name: regex
algorithm: A log filter: one compiled regex run over every line of a 50 MB log, counting the matching lines and summing the match lengths; rounds times (README.md).

skip.c: no std regex in C (POSIX regex.h is not ISO C, and the MSVC CRT has none)
skip.rust: no std regex in Rust (the regex crate is not std; no crate stands in)
skip.mk-wrap: the only arithmetic is the count, far below 2^62

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the checksum (a million per match plus its length) checks that both engines found the same matches
notes: Pattern status=5[0-9][0-9] dur=[0-9]{4,}ms: the server errors that took at least a second. All three engines (Mk std.regex, Go regexp, C# RegexOptions.NonBacktracking) are linear-time finite-automaton matchers.
